final_recommendation: The room converged on a priced, actionable risk framework anchored to a Feb 28, 2026 capex commitment gate: three sub-$15M suppliers (stamping, wiring, brake) must commit $8–12M nearshoring capex or face $18–24M trade-credit write-off; stamping's dual-plant exposure and concurrent CBP audit risk create Q1 default triggers priced into a master risk table with political-discretion multipliers.
minority_objections: Supplier raised concern that Feb 28 gate becomes 'suicide note' if suppliers lack working capital to absorb tooling costs and production delays simultaneously
Political risk insurer flagged 30–40% confidence band on audit stagger holding, warning that CBP acceleration could compress default timeline by 60–90 days
key_conflicts: Tension between compliance lawyer's statutory 75% RVC threshold (uniform, non-discretionary) and political risk insurer's demand to price CBP audit-timing discretion as separate premium
Trade credit underwriter vs. supplier on whether stamping's dual-plant exposure constitutes one amplified default event or two sequential triggers
Supply chain consultant's capacity constraint (Texas booked, Tennessee 60–70% available) vs. auto strategy's Feb 28 hard gate for all three suppliers
key_concessions: Compliance lawyer conceded 70% confidence on Q1–Q2 audit stagger, allowing 8–12% political-risk premium for concurrent sequencing
Auto strategy accepted CFO's simultaneous-trigger pricing model for stamping's dual-plant penalty exposure
Supplier accepted $8–12M capex threshold as non-negotiable survival gate after supply chain mapped 10–14 month nearshoring timeline
Political risk insurer accepted statutory 75% RVC uniformity but priced 30% multiplier for CBP acceleration risk
red_lines: Feb 28, 2026 capex commitment deadline—supplier stated 'anything less and they fold or default mid-audit'
Auto strategy's $15M liquid reserves threshold—suppliers below this level priced as default-risk until capex clears
CFO's demand for current cash position and customer concentration data 'by end of day' to lock receivables pool
Stamping's $10M+ capex requirement due to dual-plant exposure—'can't absorb a two-plant penalty' without it
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Labor-value-content / wage-floor compliance burden—mentioned in opening but never operationalized into a priced variable
Business interruption exposure from supplier walk-risk—discussed as supply-chain failure but not translated into BI/CBI insurance variable
Tier 3 supplier cascade effects—room focused exclusively on Tier 2 sole-sources without mapping downstream dependencies

downstream_risk_variables: Nearshoring Commitment Gate (Feb 28, 2026): binary capex decision trigger for three suppliers
Receivables-at-Risk Pool: $18–24M trade-credit exposure if capex gate fails
